text: Supports multiple DDS middleware implementations (Cyclone DDS, Fast DDS, Connext) that can be selected or swapped at runtime
quote: Support for multiple DDS implementations, chosen at runtime - Currently Eclipse Cyclone DDS, eProsima Fast DDS, and RTI Connext DDS are fully supported.

text: Bridge for communication between ROS 1 and ROS 2, available for topics and services but not yet for actions
quote: ROS 1 - ROS 2 communication bridge - Available for topics and services, not yet available for actions.

text: Quality of Service settings for handling non-ideal networks
quote: Quality of service settings for handling non-ideal networks

text: QoS policies tune communication from TCP-like reliable to UDP-like best-effort delivery, with many states in between
quote: With the right set of Quality of Service policies, ROS 2 can be as reliable as TCP or as best-effort as UDP, with many, many possible states in between.

text: Predefined QoS profiles for common use cases such as sensor data
quote: ROS 2 provides a set of predefined QoS profiles for common use cases (e.g. sensor data).

text: Transient-local durability lets publishers persist samples for late-joining subscribers, similar to latching
quote: Transient local: the publisher becomes responsible for persisting samples for "late-joining" subscriptions.

text: Node components can be composed at compile, link, load, or run time (C++ only)
quote: Composition of node components at compile, link, load, or run time - Currently only in C++.

text: Support for nodes with managed lifecycles (C++ only)
quote: Support for nodes with managed lifecycles - Currently only in C++.

text: Launch system for coordinating multiple nodes
quote: Launch system for coordinating multiple nodes

text: Client libraries in multiple programming languages, such as Python and C++
quote: Client libraries come in a variety of programming languages so that users may write ROS 2 code in the language that is best-suited for their application

text: Nodes written with different client libraries can exchange messages via shared code generators
quote: Nodes written using different client libraries are able to share messages with each other because all client libraries implement code generators

text: Python client interface uses native Python types and idioms like lists and context objects
quote: The interface provides an idiomatic Python experience that uses native Python types and patterns like lists and context objects.

text: Suite of command-line tools under the ros2 command for introspecting and working with nodes, topics, services, and more
quote: The main entry point for the tools is the command ros2, which itself has various sub-commands for introspecting and working with nodes, topics, services, and more.

text: Command-line introspection tools are built on an extensible framework
quote: Command-line introspection tools using an extensible framework

text: CLI topic subcommand can publish and echo messages on a topic
quote: the topic sub-command can be used to publish and echo messages on a topic.

text: Background daemon caches ROS graph information to speed up queries like listing node names
quote: ROS 2 runs a background daemon process that maintains information about the ROS graph to provide faster responses to queries, such as the list of node names.

text: ros2 doctor checks the ROS setup for potential issues
quote: doctor: Check ROS setup for potential issues

text: Tracing tools collect information on ROS node execution (Linux only)
quote: trace: Tracing tools to get information on ROS nodes execution (only available on Linux)

text: Topics provide publish/subscribe messaging for continuous data streams
quote: Topics implement a publish/subscribe pattern. A node publishes data to a topic, and other nodes subscribe to receive that data.

text: Services provide synchronous request/response interactions between clients and servers
quote: Services implement a request/response pattern. A client sends a request, and a server replies with a response.

text: Actions support long-running goals with feedback during execution, cancellation, and results
quote: Actions allow clients to send goals, receive feedback during the execution, cancel if needed, and return a result if available

text: Nodes can set and retrieve parameters
quote: Set/retrieve parameters

text: Built-in topic statistics measure subscription message behavior and publish metrics on a statistics topic
quote: When you enable topic statistics for a subscription, ROS publishes the collected data at regular intervals as a MetricsMessage on a statistics topic.

text: Content-filtering subscriptions (C++ only)
quote: Content filtering subscription - Currently only in C++.

text: Service introspection
quote: Service Introspection

text: Inter- and intra-process communication through the same API (C++ only)
quote: Inter- and intra-process communication using the same API - Currently only in C++.

text: Multiple executors at the callback-group level within the same node
quote: Multiple executors (at level of callback groups) in same node

text: Static remapping of ROS names
quote: Static remapping of ROS names

text: Preliminary support for real-time code, on Linux only
quote: Preliminary support for real-time code ... Linux only. ... Preliminary support for "bare-metal" microcontrollers

text: Preliminary support for bare-metal microcontrollers
quote: Preliminary support for "bare-metal" microcontrollers

text: Built-in security encrypts data in transit and authenticates participants across the ROS graph
quote: Built-in ROS 2 security features enable control over communications throughout the ROS graph. This not only allows for encrypting data in transit between ROS domain participants, but also enables authentication of participants sending data

text: DDS-Security support via the sros2 package
quote: The `sros2` package provides the tools and instructions to use ROS 2 on top of DDS-Security.

text: sros2 utilities create a keystore used to enable security for all participants in the graph
quote: Use the sros2 utilities to create the keystore. Files in the keystore will be used to enable security for all the participants in the ROS 2 graph.

text: Security enclaves encapsulate protection policies and can be mapped to processes, users, or devices at deployment
quote: Security enclaves can be flexibly mapped to processes, users, or devices at deployment.

text: Robot simulations can be launched with Gazebo integrated with ROS 2
quote: Goal: Launch a Simulation with Gazebo and ROS 2

text: Record and play back rosbag data files
quote: bag: Record/play a rosbag

text: Python API for reading from and writing to bags in your own code
quote: It also provides a Python API for reading from and writing to a bag from your own source code.

text: Subscribe to a topic and write received data to a bag while processing it
quote: This allows you to subscribe to a topic and save the received data to a bag at the same time as performing any other processing of your choice on that data.

text: Bags can store data from non-topic sources, such as synthetic data for training sets
quote: it is also possible to save data generated by another source than a topic, such as synthetic data for training sets.

text: Bare-bones ROS-Base install with communication libraries, message packages, and CLI tools but no GUI
quote: ROS-Base Install (Bare Bones): Communication libraries, message packages, command line tools. No GUI tools.

text: Desktop install bundles ROS, RViz visualization, demos, and tutorials
quote: Desktop Install (Recommended): ROS, RViz, demos, tutorials.

text: Set of software libraries and tools for building robot applications, from drivers to algorithms
quote: The Robot Operating System (ROS) is a set of software libraries and tools that help you build robot applications. From drivers to state-of-the-art algorithms
